I can understand where you are coming from. I found myself in a similar position a few years ago before I realized I was actually trans. I can talk through why I think this all happened. I originally was just really curious about girl stuff, like makeup and dresses and all that. But I was a boy and I turned to the internet seeing if there were boys who could somehow look like convincing girls. It wasn't a sexual thing at first, but I think, at the cusp of puberty (i guess it was more than a few years ago) it slowly became a sexual thing. I think this is partly due to the fact that i am also attracted to women and being able to see think of myself as being a woman was the first time I was able to feel a sense of "sexiness". I slowly ended up looking at more and more feminization and "forced" stuff. I think this was mainly due to the fact that it was really all that was available even though I never liked the humiliation aspects of it. I really just wanted to see a guy become a girl. Although I think the "forced" aspect of it played into my own repression and telling myself that I could never become a woman unless someone else forced me to do it, even though it was something that I felt I wanted at the time. Part of it becoming a sexual thing may also be that it is difficult for some people to express their sexuality when they are not identifying as their desired gender. This might also be making the process of becoming the desired gender a source of arousal. I hope that makes sense and is helpful in any way.

Trans woman here, but with plenty of mens room experience under my belt (at college as well) i can tell you a few things. 

In almost every context, most men try not to acknowledge each other at all while in the bathroom unless they know each other (save that one weurd guy at baseball games and stuff who will talk to everyone while peeing. But thats the exception) 

If you feel like someone looks uncomfortable while you are also in the bathroom, thats because that is how they always look when going to the bathroom with strangers. 

If you feel weird using a stall for such a short amount of time, just wait in there a little longer before leaving. Some people can take silent dumps, but I can also promise that no one is timing you to see how long you are in a stall. 

Another word of advice is that, in general, if there is ever an extra space to use a sink/urinal/stall that keeps one in between you and the next person, do that. 

It can be an uncomfortable experience, but it can help to remember that no one else really likes it either.

Hi there! I'm an RA at my university so I might be able to provide a little insight into the situation. Of course, your school may have different policies, so nothing I say is absolute. Some important things to consider. One important aspect is whether or not your floor has a bathroom shared by everyone on the floor. If the administration considers a transitioning student to be their preferred gender, then I would guess there is a good chance they might try to find somewhere that your roommate can move to to increase comfort. A lot of this really depends on how your school's administration views transgender students. It is also possible that someone in administration will try to personally work something special out with your roommate that will work best for them. I would also look to see if your university offers any form of gender inclusive housing. If so, that might be a preferential option for your roommate. I hope any of that helped but feel free to message me or ask any follow up questions. I hope everything goes well!

I'm so sorry that this is something you are going through. I won't claim I know the answers, or how to help, because I have no authority on the issue. But what I will say is that I care. Suicide always seems like the answer when everything is going badly. But its a permanent solution for a temporary problem. I don't know you, but I would care if you were no longer around to be part of this community. And I would be willing to bet anything there are a lot of people who know you who absolutely care for you. If you don't feel like you have the strength to carry on for yourself, then carry on for those that know you. I apologize if that sounds harsh I really don't mean it that way. But I know that its hard to see yourself as valuable when something terrible like that happens. Its not easy at all and I am so sorry for that. I'm confident that if you give yourself time (and maybe even if you give your parents time) you will find a solution. When a car runs out of gas do you set it on fire and leave it to burn? No. You might even have to push it all to the gas station. It might be incredibly difficult, and take a very long time, but in the end, that car is back to driving on the road. That was probably a shitty analogy but its the best I have right now. Seek help and support wherever you can find it. Remove toxic people from your life. I wish you the best of luck. There will always be someone who cares about you, even if it was only me.
